messages.content: Predict a human response in an economic game with a physically present palm-sized Cozmo robot. The human taps the blue cube to keep coins or the yellow cube to share. Cozmo chooses at the same time behind a board, so neither player sees the other’s current choice. In each round, both share: each gets 6 coins; both keep: each gets 4; human keeps and Cozmo shares: human 10, Cozmo 0; human shares and Cozmo keeps: human 0, Cozmo 10. The payoff matrix stays visible; outcomes and cumulative scores appear only after both players choose. Cozmo maintains neutral emotionality. Before formal play, practice trials require specific answers to achieve displayed goals. In formal play the stated goal is to maximize coins. Participants are told that more coins increase their chance of a £100 shopping voucher. They see five other Cozmos and hear that the best-performing robot will be used in a later study and the others’ memories/data erased. This is the story given to participants. Participation compensation is £6/hour or four course credits, with no fixed coins-to-cash conversion specified. The number of formal rounds is not announced in advance. Predict the current cube choice. Return only keep or share.

Before the game, this person reported daily robot engagement 2 on a1 (never) to 7 (daily) scale. Their 14 item negative-attitude-to-robots sum was 37 (five-point item codes, three positive emotion items reversed; possible sum 14 to 70). They endorsed 18 of 25 robot mental/capability attributes. Their earlier 15 item self/unknown-other allocation questionnaire gave mean self allocation 91.386111 and other allocation 66.841667 in questionnaire endowment units, without a documented cash conversion. They are 23 years old and reported gender female. Verified earlier formal-round outcomes (human action, Cozmo action; human coins, Cozmo coins): none yet. Before round 1, cumulative scores are human 0, Cozmo 0 coins. Choose now; Cozmo’s current choice and this round’s result are still hidden. Practice responses and failed-tap events are not supplied.

Predict the current cube choice. Return only keep or share.

Predict the current cube choice. Return only keep or share.

Cozmo chooses at the same time behind a board, so neither player sees the other’s current choice. In each round, both share: each gets 6 coins; both keep: each gets 4; human keeps and Cozmo shares: human 10, Cozmo 0; human shares and Cozmo keeps: human 0, Cozmo 10. The payoff matrix stays visible; outcomes and cumulative scores appear only after both players choose. Cozmo maintains neutral emotionality. Participants are told that more coins increase their chance of a £100 shopping voucher. They see five other Cozmos and hear that the best-performing robot will be used in a later study and the others’ memories/data erased. This is the story given to participants. Participation compensation is £6/hour or four course credits, with no fixed coins-to-cash conversion specified. The number of formal rounds is not announced in advance. Predict the current cube choice. Return only keep or share.
